about: The questions behind My alignment and the Ideology tab. Each has two sides (sides[0] and sides[1]); liberal is the index of the liberal side, or null when the question splits both parties or has no left-right side (those count in My alignment but not in the Ideology lean); axis is the compass axis it counts on, the Political Compass way (approved Nov. 25, 2026): econ (across; axisSide is the economic-left side, the one with more government in the economy) or auth (up and down; axisSide is the authoritarian side, the one with more state power over what people may do, say or consume), or null for neither. axisWeight 0.5 marks a question that leans only slightly that way, and counts half. statement is what My alignment shows (approved Nov. 25, 2026): an opinion someone might voice, answered from strongly agree to strongly disagree, half of them arguing the left side and half the right where the question has one; agree is the side Agree counts toward; label is the short, neutral wording shown with lawmakers' records, where Favor means sides[0]. q and sides stay as the question was asked, for the evidence. groups names the interest groups whose scorecard is about the question, each with the side a high rating from it favors (public/question-scores.js ratingItems); groups that rate across many topics are on no question. "added" questions are ours, for votes the quiz has no question for. Ids never change once published: rewording keeps the evidence gathered for a question; a change of meaning gets a new id.
credit: Questions modeled on the topics of iSideWith.com's political quiz (https://www.isidewith.com/political-quiz), in our own wording, with questions added for votes the quiz doesn't cover.
